summary: This is Snowflake's reference page for the ALTER PASSWORD POLICY SQL command, which modifies an existing password policy. It covers the syntax for renaming a policy, setting or unsetting password parameters (length, character requirements, age, retries, lockout time, history, comment), and setting or unsetting tags. It also lists the OWNERSHIP privilege required, and gives an example that changes PASSWORD_MAX_RETRIES to 3.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the ALTER PASSWORD POLICY command, which renames, sets, or unsets password policy parameters and tags.
key_facts: ALTER PASSWORD POLICY modifies the properties for an existing password policy.
Changes to password policy properties take effect when the next SQL query that uses the password policy runs.
PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH supports a range of 8 to 256 inclusive and defaults to 8.
PASSWORD_MAX_LENGTH must be greater than or equal to the sum of PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH, PASSWORD_MIN_UPPER_CASE_CHARS, and PASSWORD_MIN_LOWER_CASE_CHARS, and defaults to 256.
PASSWORD_MAX_AGE_DAYS supports 0 to 999 inclusive and defaults to 90, meaning the password must be changed every 90 days.
Snowflake does not recommend a PASSWORD_MAX_AGE_DAYS value of 0 for a default account-level password policy or for any user-level policy.
PASSWORD_MAX_RETRIES supports 1 to 10 inclusive and defaults to 5.
PASSWORD_LOCKOUT_TIME_MINS supports 1 to 999 inclusive and defaults to 15 minutes.
PASSWORD_HISTORY has a default of 0 and a maximum of 24, and stored passwords cannot be repeated when a user updates their password.
PASSWORD_MIN_AGE_DAYS supports 0 to 999 inclusive and defaults to 0.
PASSWORD_MIN_UPPER_CASE_CHARS and PASSWORD_MIN_LOWER_CASE_CHARS each default to 1 and support 0 to 256 inclusive.
PASSWORD_MIN_NUMERIC_CHARS defaults to 1, and PASSWORD_MIN_SPECIAL_CHARS defaults to 0; both support 0 to 256 inclusive.
Unsetting a parameter resets it to the system default, and specifying a value when unsetting returns an error.
Executing this command requires the OWNERSHIP privilege on the password policy, and operating on objects in a schema also requires USAGE on the parent database and schema.
The example runs ALTER PASSWORD POLICY password_policy_prod_1 SET PASSWORD_MAX_RETRIES = 3 after describing the policy with DESC PASSWORD POLICY.
